title: Why AI Struggles To Reuse Chip Designs
gist: AI agents can speed derivative chip design and IP reuse, but outputs often aren't physically viable, manufacturable or cost-effective, and gaps in IP data management, multi-physics optimization at RTL, and automated implementation keep humans heavily in the loop. Vendors (Keysight, Cadence, Siemens, ChipAgents, Baya, Arm, Qualcomm) describe partial wins—especially in workflow automation and verification—while end-to-end automation remains distant.

insights.claim: AI-generated chip design changes can be radically different from the prior version rather than incremental, with no correlation between versions, raising manufacturability and cost risks for derivative designs.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Derivative-chip AI tools face a trust/cost barrier; watch for vendors offering constrained, incremental generation.
insights.quote: There’s a cost of letting AI do all of these things.
insights.locator: Instead of making an incremental change

insights.claim: Chipmakers report mixed results applying AI to derivative and new chip designs, finding AI-generated solutions can be substantially different and more costly than expected and introduce new manufacturing and verification challenges.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Tempers near-term ROI expectations for AI-in-EDA revenue narratives.
insights.locator: Chipmakers are seeing mixed results

insights.claim: Text-based LLMs in chip design are mainly useful for text artifacts—specs, RTL, verification scripts and gigabyte-scale debug logs—while many non-text aspects of chip design still require humans.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: AI value in EDA concentrates in front-end/verification text tasks; physical design remains a human/tool moat.
insights.locator: At the most fundamental level, many AI tools

insights.claim: The real measure of AI success in derivative chip design will be how reliably it turns existing IP into verified, physically viable designs with less manual effort, not how quickly it generates new RTL.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Evaluate AI-EDA offerings on verified-silicon outcomes, not RTL generation speed.
insights.locator: For chip architects and design teams

insights.claim: Qualcomm says it rapidly adapted its full automotive solution to robotics on the software side, but hardware IP scaling and SoC integration still require significant human effort.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Software reuse scales; hardware reuse is the bottleneck—an opening for EDA automation vendors.
insights.quote: However, hardware IP scaling and SoC integration still require significant human effort.
insights.locator: We were rapidly adapting the automotive solution

insights.claim: Qualcomm currently builds separate architectures and hardware design variants for each product case and is asking EDA vendors for one flexible architecture that adapts across diverse requirements.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Signals demand for configurable-architecture EDA tooling from a top SoC vendor.
insights.locator: Currently, we often create separate architectures

insights.claim: Qualcomm reported three months spent tuning EDA tool recipes without changing RTL or floorplan, calling it a huge source of inefficiency, while noting AI-aided fine-tuning from EDA vendors consumes a lot of compute.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: AI-driven tool-recipe tuning is a clear pain point; compute cost of AI-EDA is a customer concern.
insights.quote: Three months were spent in recipe tuning of EDA tools
insights.locator: Three months were spent in recipe tuning

insights.claim: Camera and display blocks are similar across AI products but differ sharply in camera count, speed and power requirements, making mobile multimedia IP scaling harder than adding NPU cores.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: IP scaling difficulty varies by block type; NPUs scale more easily than multimedia.
insights.locator: Those differences can also be significant across domains

insights.claim: AI-assisted derivative design requires first capturing an organization's IP data—configurations, constraints, dependencies, prior implementations—plus IP lifecycle management software, including hardware/software bills of materials.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: IP/data-management software is a prerequisite layer that benefits from AI-EDA adoption.
insights.locator: Before AI can effectively help engineers

insights.claim: Arm built an internal platform and innovation store for sharing AI prompts, plugins and solutions across teams to propagate skills lost through acquisitions and divergent group practices.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Large chip firms are institutionalizing prompt/skill sharing; internal AI enablement is a real spend area.
insights.locator: We invested in a platform and innovation store

insights.claim: ChipAgents argues a company's tape-out methodology—its accumulated rules on cell use, PPA tradeoffs and ECO fixes—is as important as the design and must be captured as an ontology for agentic AI, with customer data kept on-prem.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Agentic EDA differentiation will hinge on capturing customer-specific methodology on-prem.
insights.quote: A company’s methodology is as important as the design
insights.locator: A company’s methodology is as important

insights.claim: Baya Systems says hand-coded crossbar networks grow by an n-squared factor in difficulty, while a tiled algorithmic fabric of identical tiles gives top-down performance guarantees and is easier to scale for derivatives.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Software-defined interconnect IP (Baya) positioned to displace hand-built crossbars in switches/AI chips.
insights.locator: For our switch customers who have been working with crossbars

insights.claim: Data movement into and out of memories and processors is one of the key performance bottlenecks, making deterministic, algorithmic interconnect optimization especially important.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Interconnect/data-movement IP remains a high-value segment.
insights.locator: While organizations wrestle with how to apply AI

insights.claim: Cadence says no tool yet optimizes timing, IR and thermal together at RTL or architecture level; current optimization starts at netlist and handles one physics at a time.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Physically-aware RTL optimization is an open gap and potential EDA product race.
insights.quote: we don’t have anything in the RTL today
insights.locator: Today, we don’t have anything that helps the RTL designer

insights.claim: ChipAgents built Build-A-Chip-Bench to evaluate AI agents from workload spec and RTL generation through synthesis, physical implementation and layout verification.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Benchmarks for end-to-end chip agents are emerging; track as a maturity signal.
insights.locator: Tool providers are addressing the challenge

insights.claim: Vinci argues the limiting chip problems now live at physical boundaries—heat flow from die to package to board, thermo-mechanical stress in heterogeneous stacks, power density versus cooling.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: System-level multi-physics simulation is a growing opportunity as chiplets/advanced packaging spread.
insights.quote: The limiting problems are no longer inside the chip
insights.locator: The limiting problems are no longer inside the chip

insights.claim: Arteris says EDA must evolve from single-die point tools to intent-centric system-level platforms spanning multi-die, packaging and HW/SW co-design, with verification complexity outpacing productivity despite AI.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Platform consolidation in EDA; verification remains the largest productivity gap.
insights.locator: EDA tools must expand beyond single-die optimization

insights.claim: Siemens reported its HyperLynx Agentic Toolkit cut design analysis for 112 high-speed channels from several weeks to a couple of hours.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Concrete agentic-EDA productivity claim; supports Siemens EDA AI monetization narrative.
insights.locator: Agentic AI tools can now shrink verification time

insights.claim: Reused, previously verified board blocks can behave differently depending on surrounding circuitry, so signal-integrity verification is still needed even for known-good blocks.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Reuse does not eliminate verification spend.
insights.locator: They verified them in the past

insights.claim: Siemens attributes agentic speedups largely to GPU and CPU cluster horsepower plus physics-based simulation engines, while implementing recommended layout changes remains largely manual.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: AI-EDA drives incremental compute demand; automated place-and-route is the next frontier.
insights.quote: Automating the actual place and route and things like that is a lot harder than automating workflow.
insights.locator: The speedup doesn’t come only from AI
